description:
**Dimension: separation-of-concerns · 1 medium finding** — see report §separation-of-concerns. Split out of `1c29a70e` on 2026-08-07 so that `07a1813a` can depend on the rename alone rather than on the whole dependency-direction bundle.

`gf2-core/src/bitvec.rs` names the Arikan (2009) coding-theory kernel on the lowest-level primitive type. Resolved 2026-08-07: rename neutrally in core rather than relocate to gf2-coding. The transform has no consumer outside gf2-core — the only references are `gf2-core/tests/polar_tests.rs` — and gf2-coding has no polar module, so relocation would create a coding-theory home with no callers. The operation itself is a generic GF(2) butterfly and belongs in core under a neutral name.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The four methods at `gf2-core/src/bitvec.rs:1496`, `:1532`, `:1593`, `:1629` are renamed to `hadamard_butterfly`, `hadamard_butterfly_into`, `hadamard_butterfly_inverse`, and `hadamard_butterfly_inverse_into`, remaining in gf2-core.
- [hard] REQ-02: All call sites are updated, including `gf2-core/tests/polar_tests.rs`; no `polar_transform` identifier survives in the workspace.
- [hard] REQ-03: No coding-theory vocabulary remains in the method names or their Rustdoc summaries; the doc prose describes a generic GF(2) butterfly. The rationale for keeping the kernel in core is recorded in the module or method Rustdoc.
- [hard] REQ-04: Behaviour is unchanged — the existing polar-transform tests pass unmodified apart from the renamed calls.
- [hard] REQ-05: `cargo nextest --profile ci`, clippy `-D warnings`, and fmt pass.

## Notes

Blocks `07a1813a`, which adds a word-level fast path to the same functions; the rename lands first so the fast path is written against the final names. Carries no parent edge by design: it is a shared-blocker node, resolved into the epic through its dependent.
title: Rename polar_transform to hadamard_butterfly in gf2-core
